RDF can be applied to support knowledge sharing in knowledge-intensive areas, such as network management and workflow, by providing a common data representation and a common ontology for data integration.

the resource description framework ( RDF ) can be extended to describe the semantics of distributed applications, such as network management systems and web services, and it can also be used to describe entities and relations within specific application domains to support knowledge sharing, ontology construction and semantic web service discovery.

the resource description framework ( RDF ) can be applied innovately to reengineer the data integration solutions in knowledge intensive areas, which were built on traditional modeling languages such as XML.

the following issues: (1) how RDF can be extended to represent knowledge-intensive application domains, (2) how RDF can support the construction of knowledge models and ontologies, and (3) how RDF can help to integrate distributed systems.
the application and extension of RDF to knowledge-intensive distributed systems, where the knowledge sharing and ontology management play a key role.

RDF can be extended and applied to support distributed knowledge-intensive applications, such as knowledge management and workflow management, in a flexible and efficient manner.

RDF can be a powerful tool for knowledge representation in distributed applications, and can help in the construction and maintenance of knowledge-intensive systems.
